title: SYSK Live: Andre the Giant
summary: Live recording at Plaza Live in Orlando, Florida, in which Josh and Chuck tell the life story of wrestler Andre the Giant (born Andre René Roussimoff in France). Covers his childhood and early rugby and wrestling career, his personas (Monster Roussimoff, Monster Eiffel Tower, Jean Ferré/Géant Ferré), his rise under Vince McMahon Sr. and the WWWF, his enormous size and acromegaly (including declining treatment), his heavy drinking, his acting roles (The Princess Bride, The Six Million Dollar Man, B.J. and the Bear), his back surgery at Vince McMahon Jr.'s urging, WrestleMania III against Hulk Hogan, and his death of heart failure in Paris in 1993 followed by his induction as the first WWE Hall of Fame inductee. Also includes opening banter, a dedication to a listener's grandmother, and ad breaks.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening remarks
segments.summary: Josh promotes upcoming SYSK Live shows in San Francisco and Sketch Fest, then Josh and Chuck open the Orlando show and dedicate it to Alice Harrison, Jamie's grandmother.

segments.title: Andre's early life in France
segments.summary: Andre René Roussimoff is born in Coulommiers, France and raised on a family farm in Molien. He grows to giant size as a child, leaves school at fourteen for Paris, and works moving furniture. A tidbit about Samuel Beckett giving rides is noted as unverified.

segments.title: Rugby, entry into wrestling, and personas
segments.summary: Andre joins rugby, is recruited by wrestlers at his gym, and begins touring as a pro wrestler in Japan, Africa and New Zealand. He wrestles under names including Monster Roussimoff, Monster Eiffel Tower, and Jean Ferré, a play on the French folk hero Grand Ferré.

segments.title: Return home and Vince McMahon Sr.
segments.summary: Hosts recount a legend of Andre returning to his parents in a Rolls-Royce as Géant Ferré. Eduard Carpentier takes him to Quebec and introduces him to Vince McMahon Sr., who builds his national career by moving him region to region.

segments.title: Size, the name Andre the Giant, and strength
segments.summary: Andre debuts at Madison Square Garden in 1973 as Andre the Giant, billed as the eighth Wonder of the World. Height and weight are disputed, wrist size and boot size are compared, and feats of strength such as moving cars and lifting weights are described.

segments.title: Interpreter, friends, and rivals
segments.summary: Andre's limited English and speech difficulties from his condition are discussed, along with his interpreter Frank Valois, his small circle of true friends, and his feuds with Big John Studd, The Iron Sheik, and Randy Macho Man Savage.

segments.title: Ring antics and the King of the Cage
segments.summary: Andre pulls hair from Randy Savage and plays pranks on fellow wrestlers such as Hacksaw Jim Duggan. He becomes known as the King of the Cage match, is one of the highest paid wrestlers, and is described as one of the most recognizable sports figures of his era.

segments.title: Mid-show break
segments.summary: Short break between segments with a host joke about a message break.

segments.title: TV and film appearances
segments.summary: Andre appears on The Six Million Dollar Man, B.J. and the Bear, The Destroyer, a Honeycomb cereal commercial, and a Cyndi Lauper video. Lee Majors' reaction to his stunt is discussed, and his affection for The Princess Bride is noted.

segments.title: Drinking, acromegaly, and declining treatment
segments.summary: Andre's heavy drinking is described, with estimates of up to fifty-two beers a day and a record of 156 beers in one sitting. His acromegaly diagnosis in Japan and later at Duke University is covered, along with his refusal of treatment and the difficulties his size caused in daily life.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short ad break and hosts' banter.

segments.title: Ranch in North Carolina, fish camp, and loneliness
segments.summary: Andre's ranch in Ellerby, North Carolina is described along with his Florida fish camp, Giants Fish Camp in Sarasota area. A family member's memory of him is shared. Andre expresses a wish for a normal life and says children were often afraid of him.

segments.title: The Princess Bride
segments.summary: Andre is cast in The Princess Bride after Rob Reiner hires him. Co-star struggles with drinking on set are mentioned, along with his nervousness at the Toronto premiere, his VHS copy, and his enjoyment of the film. Back injuries affect his stunt work.

segments.title: Back surgery, WrestleMania III, and final years
segments.summary: Vince McMahon Jr. persuades Andre to undergo back surgery in England. Andre returns for WrestleMania III in Detroit, where he and Hulk Hogan face off and Hogan wins. Andre later wrestles in Japan and Mexico and in tag matches using his partners for support.

segments.title: Death in Paris and legacy
segments.summary: Andre dies of heart failure in a Paris hotel in 1993, two weeks after his father's funeral. His body is flown to North Carolina, he is the first WWE Hall of Fame inductee, and the annual Andre the Giant Battle Royal honors him. His daughter Robin and his estate are discussed.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the show, plug the podcast network, and thank the audience.
